campaign: Agent memory 0.7.1 follow-ups (M71): hand mutants of slices S2 to S6
protocol: Each mutant replaces exactly one occurrence of `old` by `new` in `file` of `baseline_commit`; a record with `edits` makes every replacement it lists, in order, and has no top-level `old` or `new`. `old` and `new` use LF line breaks: convert them to the line endings of the checkout (CRLF in a Windows working tree). `cmd` runs from the repository root. A mutant is killed when the build succeeds and at least one test the command ran fails because of it; `failing_tests` names up to five of them and `failed_tests_recorded` counts the recorded ones (the runner kept at most 12). A build error, a crash or a command that runs no test is not a kill. A mutant is equivalent when the build succeeds, every test the command ran passes, and `argument` shows that no input tells it from the original. The file is restored before the next mutant. `ran_on` is `slice campaign` for a result recorded when the slice's campaign ran (on the lane head of that slice) and `baseline_commit` for a mutant re-expressed for, and re-run on, that commit. Every `old` was re-checked to occur exactly once in `baseline_commit`, and every failing test named here still exists there.

S2.scope: binding record codec and grants digest, identity and rotation rules, startup plan and legacy adoption, record write, server start and reservations, recheck of every mutation

S3.scope: raw reserved-name guard: label and key predicates, every operation kind, and the graph batch route

S4.scope: cosine distance for exact and mmr recall: metric, candidate pool, reported distance, zero-norm refusal

S5.scope: exact recall with text: validity rule, fused candidates, explanation, budgets, adapter refusals

S6.scope: evidence references on remember items: reserved record ids, storage token, raw-access 403, attachment, forget, and the repeated-item rule

mutants.argument: With the mutant a string of any length is collected into `text`, and the checks that follow refuse every case the removed guard refused. All eleven required properties must be present (`get(name)?` fails otherwise) and each is checked by a rule that only a short value satisfies: the four schema and version properties must equal a fixed constant (the longest is 24 bytes); `generation`, `receipt_window_ms` and the optional `retired_at_ms` go through `canonical`, which refuses more than 20 bytes; `state` must be `active` or `retired` (and `retired_at_ms` is allowed only with `retired`); `grants_digest` must be exactly 67 bytes (`digest_shaped`); `tenant` must be `@root` or 32 hex digits (`valid_tenant`); `binding` and the optional `evidence` are collection names of at most 63 bytes (`valid_collection_name`); `graph` is a graph name of at most 63 bytes (`validate_graph_name`). A property outside the accepted set is refused by the unknown-property check, and a value that is not a string by the `_ => return Err(Corrupt)` arm of the loop, whatever the length. So an oversized string in any property still ends in `Err(Corrupt)`, the value the removed guard returned; the guard is a redundant first line of defence. Separately the engine refuses to store a string above 4,096 bytes at all (`validate_value`), so a node written through the API cannot carry one.
